subject: Renewal + Expansion — tactical redline playbook and sign path
messages:
From: Avery Systems Legal <legal@averysys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion paperwork — initial redlines

Marissa / team,

Thanks for the renewal package. We reviewed the MSA+order form and attached our redlines (see Avery_MSA_Redlines_20260818.docx). High level items we cannot sign as-is:

- Indemnity: narrow the third-party claims carveouts and add reciprocal breach language.
- SLA credit cap: request removing the 3x cap for production outages affecting >5% of calls.
- Data residency: need explicit EU residency guarantee for logs associated with EU tenants.
- Change of control: propose 90-day notice vs 30 days.

We'd like to protect the uptick pricing for the first renewal term (12 months) while committing to the +40% capacity uplift. Please confirm whether Redwood can accept the indemnity wording in §8, and whether order form v3 can show a step-down credit for SLA breaches.

Attached: Avery_MSA_Redlines_20260818.docx

Regards,
Sam Park
Sr. Counsel — Avery Systems

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Avery Systems Legal <legal@averysys.com>, Sam Park <sam.park@averysys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T18:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion paperwork — initial redlines

Sam — thanks for the clear list and the doc. Appreciate the quick read.

We've pulled legal in line and sketched a pragmatic path so we don't introduce signature delays for the expansion. High-level plan:

1) Indemnity: Redwood legal proposes a compromise — reciprocal breach indemnity plus a negotiated third-party carveout limited to intellectual property claims tied to prior versions. Karthik, see draft language attached.
2) SLA credits: we can remove the 3x hard cap for material outages if Avery accepts a graduated credit schedule (OrderForm_Avery_v3.pdf) and a max aggregate credit equal to one month's subscription in a 12-month rolling window.
3) Data residency: we can commit to EU residency for logs and audit data for EU accounts if customer provides a signed addendum and accepts the private-region routing fee.
4) Change of control: can move to 60 days (split the delta).

Next asks for you Sam: please flag any redlines that are absolute blockers vs negotiable. For internal ops: Vanessa — can procurement absorb the private-region routing fee in the quote? Karthik — can you review the indemnity draft and advise whether we should accept the IP carveout as written.

I'll pull together a short "tactical redline playbook" for our legal and the sign path (DocuSign recommended). I also want to avoid simultaneous re-negotiation on price while we fix the MSA — the order form should capture the +40% capacity uplift at existing per-token rates for the first 12 months.

Attachments: OrderForm_Avery_v3.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Renewals — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:11:00Z
Subject: INTERNAL: tactical playbook + ask log for Avery renewal (please prioritize)

Karthik / Vanessa — quick internal note before I respond to Sam.

Key asks:
- Legal: confirm acceptability of reciprocal breach + limited IP carveout. If you think the IP carveout is risky, propose alternative (e.g., $X liability cap carveout or insurance-backed solution).
- Finance/Procurement (Vanessa): can we quote the private-region routing fee as a one-time setup vs recurring? Also need confirmation on whether we can trade a 1-month credit cap (for SLA) for stricter SLO definitions.
- Sales: confirm that the +40% capacity uplift and fixed per-token during the first 12 months is locked in the order form. No further commercial repricing during that period.

I'm attaching a short checklist I'm going to send to Avery to accelerate closure: 1) final MSA redline summary, 2) order form with credit ladder, 3) DocuSign sign path with single signature from Avery + Redwood business signatory, 4) PO instructions for Avery procurement.

Can you both send quick comments by EOD PST? I'm prepared to escalate to legal head if we need an exception on indemnity.

-Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: tactical playbook + ask log for Avery renewal (please prioritize)

Marissa — quick read from legal.

- Reciprocal breach indemnity: acceptable.
- IP carveout: we should narrow the scope — allow IP claims tied to modifications made by Avery to our model outputs and remove open-ended ongoing liability. Suggest adding a $5M aggregate cap applicable only to IP claims (outside general liability cap). That gives Avery comfort while protecting Redwood.
- SLA credit ladder: acceptable if we keep an overall monetary cap (1 month equivalent) and add a 30-day cure period for non-chronic incidents.
- Data residency: we can sign an addendum committing to EU residency for logs provided routing is in our EU region pool and a modest per-GB replication fee. No vendor lock.

If you want legal sign-off for the compromise language, I can prepare the redline and route to our GC for approval (24–36 hours). If Avery pushes for complete removal of the IP cap we should escalate.

-Karthik
Legal Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion paperwork — commercial sign path and PO

Sam / team, Marissa — quick procurement note.

We can present the private-region routing fee as a one-time setup charge and absorb the first 10GB of daily replication for free as a commercial concession for the expansion. After that, pricing will be per-GB in the order form appendix. I'll update OrderForm_Avery_v3.pdf to reflect the one-time fee and the free trial slice.

PO process: Avery can either provide a PO referencing RDW-DEAL-9271 or sign via DocuSign (preferred for fastest execution). I'll be the Redwood signee for commercial. If Avery needs net-60 payment terms, we'll need finance approval; otherwise net-30 standard applies.

I'll post an updated order form tonight and the DocuSign envelope link tomorrow morning.

-Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Procurement & Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion paperwork — tactical redline playbook and sign path

Sam — thanks for the redlines and for the quick sync. Per our internal review we propose the following execution path to avoid rework and close this week:

1) Redwood will produce a clean MSA redline that implements the reciprocal breach indemnity, the narrowed IP carveout with a $5M aggregate cap, and the 60-day change-of-control notice. (Karthik to produce final redline — 24 hours).
2) Redwood & Avery agree to the SLA credit ladder (no 3x uncapped multiplier). Aggregate credits capped at one month of subscription in any 12-month period; 30-day cure window for chronic issues.
3) Avery to confirm acceptance of the EU data residency addendum; upon email confirmation Redwood will attach the addendum to the DocuSign envelope. Private-region routing fee shown as one-time in order form; first 10GB of replication waived.
4) DocuSign sign path: Avery business signatory -> Redwood commercial signee (Vanessa). Link: https://www.docusign.com/embeddedSigning/abc123

If you confirm by EOD PT we'll send the DocuSign envelope with the redline and order form. Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Marissa
